issues.description: Transform is not applied when splitting via delimiter
issues.detail: The new delimiter branch in get_param_as_list assigns items = items.split(...) but does not run the resulting strings through the transform callable. The later code path applies transform only when items is already a list from auto_parse_qs_csv or multiple instances. A caller passing both transform and delimiter will get raw strings, inconsistent with documented behavior.

issues.description: Empty/blank elements from delimiter split are not filtered or documented
issues.detail: str.split(',') on 'a,,b' yields ['a','','b'], and split(' ') on 'a  b' yields ['a','','b']. The docstring notes that keep_blank_qs_values has no effect on secondary splitting, but does not specify whether blanks are kept. There are no tests for adjacent delimiters, leading/trailing delimiters, or empty values.

issues.description: ValueError raised for bad delimiter bypasses HTTPBadRequest contract
issues.detail: Other invalid-input paths in get_param_as_list raise HTTPBadRequest (e.g., when transform raises ValueError). Raising a bare ValueError for an unsupported delimiter is a programmer error scenario, but it is surprising relative to the method's documented Raises section and is not mentioned in the new docstring. Consider documenting it explicitly or validating once at call setup.

issues.description: Docstring versionadded directive sits inside the delimiter argument block
issues.detail: The `.. versionadded:: 4.3` directive is nested inside the delimiter parameter description rather than at the method/argument level convention used elsewhere in falcon. This may render oddly in Sphinx output and is inconsistent with surrounding docstring style. Verify the rendered HTML matches the project's documentation conventions.

issues.description: Silent no-op when delimiter is specified but param arrived as list
issues.detail: When a param is repeated (?x=a&x=b) and the caller passes delimiter='|', the delimiter is silently ignored. The docstring mentions this, but there is no test asserting per-element splitting is not attempted (e.g., ?x=a|b&x=c|d returns ['a|b','c|d']). Worth a regression test to lock in the documented behavior.

issues.description: Delimiter lookup table conflates aliases with literals awkwardly
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS maps ',', '|', ' ' to themselves alongside the OAS symbolic names. This works but means any future single-char delimiter must be added to the dict to be accepted. A cleaner design would be a set of literals plus an alias map; minor maintainability concern.

review.summary: The delimiter feature is small and well-scoped, but the splitting path bypasses the transform callable, which is likely a latent bug for callers combining delimiter with transform. Blank/empty handling after splitting is unspecified and untested for edge cases like adjacent or trailing delimiters. The ValueError for unsupported delimiters diverges from the method's HTTPBadRequest convention and is undocumented in the Raises section. Tests cover the happy paths well but miss the list-already-present no-op and empty-element cases.
